summary: NEXUS is an interactive space mission design and simulation game that lets users experience the challenges of planning and carrying out space missions. Players can choose destinations such as Earth orbit, the Moon, Mars, and other orbital paths, assemble spacecraft, select rockets, and manage mission resources including fuel, power, mass, and communication. After completing mission checks, users launch their spacecraft and experience a simulated journey through different phases of flight. NEXUS also includes mission results, replay options, and multiplayer features that allow users to experience missions together. The project aims to make space exploration more engaging and accessible through interactive gameplay and simplified educational simulations.
details:
How NEXUS Works

NEXUS is an interactive space mission simulation game designed to introduce users to the process of planning and executing space missions.

Users begin by selecting a mission destination, such as Earth orbit, the Moon, Mars, or other orbital paths. They then choose a rocket and assemble their spacecraft by configuring different components.

Before launch, the system checks important mission resources and conditions, including mass, power, fuel, and communication capabilities. Users must complete the mission readiness checks before proceeding with the launch sequence.

The simulation includes a countdown, rocket ascent, stage separation, and different spaceflight phases. After the mission, users can review the results and replay their experience.

NEXUS also provides additional exploration and experimentation features, including a universe exploration section, a sandbox, a mission catalog, saved missions, and multiplayer functionality.

Educational Purpose

The goal of NEXUS is to make space exploration more accessible and engaging. By combining interactive gameplay with simplified spaceflight concepts, the project encourages users to explore mission planning, spacecraft systems, and the challenges of space exploration.

NEXUS is an educational simulation, not a professional spacecraft flight-planning tool. Its calculations and representations are simplified for learning and entertainment.
